trainer: ChatGPT writes the script. The host runs it.

items.name: RunPod
items.why: Best overall. Pods, templates, per-second billing, no egress on the main product.

items.name: Vast.ai
items.why: Cheapest wide catalog. Good for interruptible LoRA. Watch bandwidth fees.

items.name: Lambda
items.why: Clean datacenter GPUs. Better when the run must finish.

items.name: Modal
items.why: Code-first and scale-to-zero. Best when ChatGPT writes a Python script.

items.name: Paperspace
items.why: Notebooks and a gentle start. Pricier than the GPU specialists.

items.name: Google Colab
items.why: Fastest beginner start. Free tier is enough for a tiny LoRA smoke test.

items.name: Lightning AI
items.why: Studios and training jobs. Easy if you want a notebook plus a run.

items.name: Together AI
items.why: Managed open models and GPU jobs. Less ops.

items.name: CoreWeave
items.why: High quality clusters. Best for large reliable runs, not a first LoRA.

items.name: Nebius
items.why: Self-serve GPU cloud with InfiniBand on bigger nodes.

items.name: Crusoe
items.why: Datacenter GPUs, energy-backed capacity. Mid convenience.

items.name: Hyperstack
items.why: Simple GPU VMs. Good middle price if stock is there.

items.name: Massed Compute
items.why: Budget datacenter cards. Fine for batch fine-tunes.

items.name: Lium
items.why: Marketplace prices. Check stock before you rely on a quote.

items.name: Jarvislabs
items.why: Fast spin-up notebooks. Convenient for short trains.

items.name: DataCrunch
items.why: European GPU cloud. Straightforward hourly rental.

items.name: TensorDock
items.why: Marketplace GPUs. Cheap if you can restart.

items.name: Thunder Compute
items.why: Low-friction cheap GPUs for experiments.

items.name: Salad
items.why: Distributed cheap GPUs. Best for batch, not a live class.

items.name: Replicate
items.why: Easiest hosted run if you already have a model. More inference than training.

items.name: Hugging Face Jobs
items.why: Runs next to your model repo. Convenient if the weights already live there.

items.name: Baseten
items.why: Deploy and some training. Better after the adapter exists.

items.name: Fal
items.why: Fast inference hosting. Use after distill, not for the first train.

items.name: AWS
items.why: Highest convenience if you already live there. Usually the expensive default.

items.name: Google Cloud
items.why: Good if you need GCP services with the GPU. Not the cheap path.

items.name: Azure
items.why: Good if the org is already on Azure. Not the first choice for a solo LoRA.

items.name: Oracle Cloud
items.why: Sometimes the value pick. Account limits are the catch.

items.name: DigitalOcean
items.why: Simple VMs. Small GPU catalog.

items.name: Scaleway
items.why: European option with a small GPU list.

items.name: Your own desktop
items.why: Free after you own the card. Best efficiency if a 24 GB GPU is already on the desk.
